name: David George
summary: David George appears in Part 9, Part 10 of The Buildout. Part 9: Habit Was the Moat. Agents Are Draining It.; Part 10: The Bubble Is in the Denominator. Argued in Part 9 (Still a demo), Part 9 (The owner of the agent), Part 10 (Still renting at January prices).

parts.headline: Habit Was the Moat. Agents Are Draining It.
The Bubble Is in the Denominator

mentions.excerpt: David George, Sternstein’s colleague, counts barely 2% of US households paying for an AI service as of April.
David George sees a Red Queen’s Race at the model layer: switching is easy down to the task, so distribution and the ability to create new kinds of customers matter more than price.
Michael Howell of Capital Wars says he underestimated AI spending’s lift to earnings; David George at a16z credits technology with about 76% of S&P 500 profit growth through late August.
David George says rental rates and residual values were supposed to fall but have not; A100 rental prices are no lower than in January.

sides.claim: The creators argue OpenAI will prevail not because of best models, chips, cost-performance curve or even best product — though they think OpenAI has those — but because it is so good at creating new kinds of customers and has the most durable…

As of September 2026, the creators say intelligence-as-a-service product rankings are no longer the most important question; intelligence is everywhere and nearly anyone can do nearly anything, yet most people aren't yet, so awakening new behavior…

sides.question: who-collects
sides.claim: As of April, barely about 2% of US households were paying for some AI service; the number is higher now and growing, but still tiny in the big scheme of things.

sides.question: who-collects
sides.claim: While nearly 30% of S&P 500 companies report some quantifiable impact of AI, only about 2% report any tracked metric, and similarly only a tiny share of the overall userbase is meaningfully deploying agentic use-cases at scale.
Since 2023, tech has been the earnings growth story, contributing about 76% of the S&P 500's total earnings growth in 2026 as of late August.
